summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma, was admitted with recurrent fevers and found to have acute cholecystitis with a contained gallbladder rupture. He underwent percutaneous cholecystostomy tube placement, which drained purulent material. Post-procedure, he developed fevers, rigors, and a lactate of 5.5, consistent with severe sepsis, and was transferred to the ICU. Blood and gallbladder cultures confirmed E. coli infection, which showed intermediate sensitivity to meropenem. Antibiotics were switched to tigecycline, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient IV therapy. His condition improved with treatment, and he was discharged home to complete a 7-day course of tigecycline, with follow-up arranged for drain management and oncology care.
